ucs.title: [LLM] Salt Typhoon (Earth Estries / GhostEmperor) DLL side-loading chain — non-Microsoft signed loader in ProgramData/Public + adjacent unsigned D
ucs.description: Hunts the Salt Typhoon signature loader pattern: a legitimately signed third-party binary (Trend Micro, Norman, Symantec, McAfee, Adobe, etc.) executed from a non-standard directory (ProgramData, Users\Public, AppData\Local\Temp, PerfLogs, Windows\Temp), followed within minutes by an adjacent same-folder DLL load whose hash differs from the loader. This is the documented Demodex / Crowdoor / GhostSpider / SnappyBee (Deed RAT) delivery chain attributed to G1045 across Earth Estries telco intrusions.
ucs.splunk: | tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_path="*\\ProgramData\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\Users\\Public\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\PerfLogs\\*" OR Processes.process_path="*\\Windows\\Temp\\*") Processes.user!="*$" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process_path Processes.process_hash Processes.process_id Processes.process_guid _time | rename Processes.* as * | eval loader_dir=replace(process_path,"\\\\[^\\\\]+$","") | join type=inner dest process_guid [ | tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name="*.dll" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.process_guid Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_hash _time | rename Filesystem.* as * | eval dll_dir=replace(file_path,"\\\\[^\\\\]+$","") | rename _time as dll_time ] | where loader_dir==dll_dir AND file_hash!=process_hash AND (dll_time>=_time AND dll_time<=_time+300) | search [ | inputlookup signed_publisher_vendors.csv | fields publisher ] | table firstTime dest user process_name process_path process_hash file_name file_path file_hash | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
ucs.kql:
let _suspectDirs = dynamic([@"\ProgramData\", @"\Users\Public\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\", @"\PerfLogs\", @"\Windows\Temp\"]);
let _vendorCos = dynamic(["Trend Micro","TrendMicro","Norman","Symantec","NortonLifeLock","Norton","Bitdefender","ESET","Kaspersky","McAfee","Avast","AVG","Sophos","Adobe","VMware","Citrix","Lenovo","Acer","Realtek"]);
let Loaders = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where FolderPath has_any (_suspectDirs)
    | where isnotempty(ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName)
    | where ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName !has "Microsoft"
    | where ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName has_any (_vendorCos)
    | project LoaderTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, LoaderId=ProcessId, LoaderCreate=ProcessCreationTime, LoaderPath=FolderPath, LoaderName=FileName, LoaderSHA256=SHA256, LoaderCo=ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName, AccountName;
Loaders
| join kind=inner (
    DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName endswith ".dll"
  ) on $left.DeviceId == $right.DeviceId, $left.LoaderId == $right.InitiatingProcessId
| where Timestamp between (LoaderTime .. LoaderTime + 5m)
| where FolderPath =~ LoaderPath              // DLL co-resident with loader
| where SHA256 != LoaderSHA256                // not the loader itself
| where InitiatingProcessSHA256 == LoaderSHA256
| project LoaderTime, DllLoadTime=Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, LoaderName, LoaderPath, LoaderCo, LoaderSHA256, SideLoadedDll=FileName, SideLoadedDllSHA256=SHA256
| order by LoaderTime desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
let _suspectDirs = dynamic([@"\ProgramData\", @"\Users\Public\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\", @"\PerfLogs\", @"\Windows\Temp\"]);
let _vendorCos = dynamic(["Trend Micro","TrendMicro","Norman","Symantec","NortonLifeLock","Norton","Bitdefender","ESET","Kaspersky","McAfee","Avast","AVG","Sophos","Adobe","VMware","Citrix","Lenovo"]);
WindowsEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Provider == "Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon"
| where EventID == 7                          // ImageLoad
| extend Image       = tostring(EventData.Image),
         ImageLoaded = tostring(EventData.ImageLoaded),
         Signed      = tostring(EventData.Signed),
         SigStatus   = tostring(EventData.SignatureStatus),
         LoaderHashes= tostring(EventData.Hashes),
         User        = tostring(EventData.User),
         Publisher   = tostring(EventData.Company)
| where User !endswith "$"
| where Image has_any (_suspectDirs)
| where ImageLoaded endswith ".dll"
| extend LoaderDir = extract(@"(.*\\)[^\\]+$", 1, Image)
| extend DllDir    = extract(@"(.*\\)[^\\]+$", 1, ImageLoaded)
| where LoaderDir =~ DllDir                   // DLL adjacent to loader
| where Signed == "false" or SigStatus !~ "Valid"
| join kind=inner (
    WindowsEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where Provider == "Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon"
    | where EventID == 1                      // ProcessCreate of the loader itself
    | extend Image = tostring(EventData.Image),
             ProcCompany = tostring(EventData.Company)
    | where ProcCompany has_any (_vendorCos)
    | where ProcCompany !has "Microsoft"
    | project Computer, Image, ProcCompany
  ) on Computer, Image
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, User, Image, ProcCompany, ImageLoaded, Signed, SigStatus

ucs.title: [LLM] Salt Typhoon Exchange/IIS web shell post-exploitation — w3wp.exe spawns recon LOLBins or shell interpreter
ucs.description: Hunts the post-exploitation pattern Salt Typhoon uses after dropping a China Chopper / SparrowDoor / variant web shell on Internet-facing Microsoft Exchange and IIS edge servers (T1505.003): the IIS worker process w3wp.exe directly spawning cmd/powershell/wmic and host-recon LOLBins (whoami, quser, nltest, net, ipconfig, systeminfo, tasklist, certutil, bitsadmin). This is the documented initial-foothold-to-recon hop across Earth Estries telco breaches and FamousSparrow government targets.
ucs.splunk: | tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.process_path) as image from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name=w3wp.exe Processes.process_name IN (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, pwsh.exe, wmic.exe, net.exe, net1.exe, whoami.exe, quser.exe, ipconfig.exe, systeminfo.exe, tasklist.exe, nltest.exe, arp.exe, nbtstat.exe, reg.exe, certutil.exe, bitsadmin.exe, dsquery.exe, ntdsutil.exe, csvde.exe, sc.exe, schtasks.exe) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.parent_process_id Processes.process_name | rename Processes.* as * | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
ucs.kql:
let _shellChildren = dynamic(["cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wmic.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","whoami.exe","quser.exe","ipconfig.exe","systeminfo.exe","tasklist.exe","nltest.exe","arp.exe","nbtstat.exe","reg.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","dsquery.exe","ntdsutil.exe","csvde.exe","sc.exe","schtasks.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "w3wp.exe"
| where FileName in~ (_shellChildren)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| extend AppPool = extract(@"-ap\s+\"?([^\"\s]+)\"?", 1, InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, AppPool,
          ChildImage = FolderPath, ChildName = FileName, ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ParentSHA256 = InitiatingProcessSHA256,
          IsInitiatingProcessRemoteSession
| order by Timestamp desc

let _shellChildren = dynamic(["cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wmic.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","whoami.exe","quser.exe","ipconfig.exe","systeminfo.exe","tasklist.exe","nltest.exe","arp.exe","nbtstat.exe","reg.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","dsquery.exe","ntdsutil.exe","csvde.exe","sc.exe","schtasks.exe"]);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith @"\w3wp.exe"
| extend ChildName = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, @"\")[-1]))
| where ChildName in (_shellChildren)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, SubjectUserName,
          ChildImage = NewProcessName, ChildName, ChildCmd = CommandLine,
          ParentImage = ParentProcessName,
          TokenElevationType, LogonId

title: Salt Typhoon IIS Web Shell Post-Exploit — w3wp.exe Spawns Shell Interpreter or Recon LOLBin
id: 7b3c1a14-8e21-4d77-9d2b-saltt0001
status: experimental
description: Detects IIS worker (w3wp.exe) directly spawning command interpreters or host-recon LOLBins. Characteristic of Salt Typhoon (Earth Estries / GhostEmperor / FamousSparrow, G1045) post-exploitation after web-shell drop on Internet-facing Exchange and IIS servers.
references:
  - https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G1045/
  - https://www.trendmicro.com/en_us/research/24/h/earth-estries-uses-zingdoor-snappybee-for-telco-targeting.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/18
tags:
  - attack.initial_access

  - attack.t1190

  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.t1059.003
  - attack.t1087.002

  - attack.g1045
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\w3wp.exe'
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\wmic.exe'
      - '\net.exe'
      - '\net1.exe'
      - '\whoami.exe'
      - '\quser.exe'
      - '\ipconfig.exe'
      - '\systeminfo.exe'
      - '\tasklist.exe'
      - '\nltest.exe'
      - '\arp.exe'
      - '\nbtstat.exe'
      - '\reg.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
      - '\dsquery.exe'
      - '\ntdsutil.exe'
      - '\csvde.exe'
      - '\sc.exe'
      - '\schtasks.exe'
  filter_machine_acct:
    User|endswith: '$'
  condition: selection and not filter_machine_acct
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate in-app shellouts from poorly architected web applications (allowlist by AppPool)
  - Web-based administration consoles (Exchange ECP scripts using PowerShell)
level: high
